blocks.content: CHAPTER 18: NATURAL VEGETATION & WILDLIFE OF INDIA

Natural vegetation and wildlife represent the living natural resources of India. This chapter explains how climate, rainfall, soil, relief and altitude together decide what type of forests grow in India and what kind of animals survive there. India is one of the 17 mega-biodiversity countries of the world. This chapter is VERY IMPORTANT for  because questions are asked directly from forest types, distribution, trees, animals, conservation acts and reserves.
PART A: CONCEPT OF NATURAL VEGETATION

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Natural vegetation in India is divided into five primary types: Tropical Evergreen, Tropical Deciduous, Thorn Forests and Scrubs, Montane, and Mangrove forests.
Tropical Deciduous Forests are highlighted as the most important classification of forest vegetation in India.
Mangrove Forests are also classified and referred to as Tidal Forests.
Comprehensive conservation strategies focus on identifying causes of wildlife depletion and enforcing protective measures.

blocks.content: Meaning of Natural Vegetation

Natural vegetation refers to plant life that grows naturally without human interference. It includes forests, grasslands and shrubs which have adapted themselves to the local environment. Natural vegetation differs from cultivated crops which are grown by humans.
Importance of Natural Vegetation
Natural vegetation maintains ecological balance, regulates climate, prevents soil erosion, supports wildlife, provides raw materials and helps in rainfall formation.
Factors Affecting Natural Vegetation

Natural vegetation depends mainly on climate. Rainfall, temperature, soil, relief, altitude and slope determine the type and density of vegetation. Human activities such as deforestation and afforestation also influence vegetation.
PART B: CLASSIFICATION OF NATURAL VEGETATION IN INDIA
Tropical Evergreen Forests

Tropical evergreen forests are found in regions where annual rainfall exceeds 200 cm and temperature remains high throughout the year. These forests have dense vegetation and trees do not shed leaves at the same time.
Distribution: Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Northeastern states like Assam, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh.
Characteristics: Multi-layered forests, dense canopy, little sunlight reaches ground. Important Trees: Ebony, Mahogany, Rosewood, Rubber.
Wildlife: Elephant, monkey, birds, insects.
Tropical Deciduous Forests (MOST IMPORTANT)
Tropical deciduous forests are the most widespread forests in India. These forests shed leaves during dry season to conserve moisture.
Types:

items:
• Moist Deciduous Forests – Rainfall 100–200 cm.
  • Dry Deciduous Forests – Rainfall 70–100 cm.

blocks.content: Distribution: Central India, Eastern slopes of Western Ghats, foothills of Himalayas.
Trees: Teak, Sal, Shisham, Bamboo. Wildlife: Tiger, lion, deer, elephant.
Thorn Forests and Scrubs
Thorn forests develop in areas with rainfall less than 70 cm. Trees have long roots, thick bark and small leaves to reduce water loss.
Distribution: Rajasthan, Gujarat, parts of Punjab and Haryana. Trees: Babool, Kikar, Date palm.
Wildlife: Camel, desert fox, snakes.
Montane Forests
Montane forests are found in mountainous regions. Vegetation changes with altitude due to temperature variation.
Lower Slopes: Broad-leaved trees like oak and chestnut. Higher Slopes: Coniferous trees like pine, deodar, fir.
Very High Altitude: Alpine vegetation. Wildlife: Snow leopard, yak, bear.
Mangrove Forests (Tidal Forests)
Mangrove forests grow in coastal tidal regions and river deltas. They can survive in saline water and muddy soil.
Special Feature: Aerial roots for breathing.
Distribution: Sundarbans, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna deltas. Trees: Sundari.
Wildlife: Royal Bengal Tiger, crocodile.
PART C: WILDLIFE OF INDIA
Meaning of Wildlife
Wildlife includes all animals, birds, reptiles, insects and aquatic organisms living in natural habitats.
Major Wildlife Species of India
India has a rich variety of wildlife such as tiger (national animal), lion (Gir forest), elephant, rhinoceros (Assam), leopard, deer, camel, peacock (national bird).
Causes of Wildlife Depletion

items: Tropical Deciduous Forests are explicitly designated as the most important topic for competitive examination questions.
Mangrove Forests are frequently tested under their alternate title: Tidal Forests.

blocks.content: Deforestation, poaching, habitat destruction, urbanisation, pollution and climate change are major causes of decline in wildlife population.
PART D: CONSERVATION OF NATURAL VEGETATION & WILDLIFE
Need for Conservation
Conservation is necessary to maintain ecological balance, protect endangered species and ensure sustainable development.
Conservation Measures

Protected areas such as national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves help in conservation. Government initiatives like Project Tiger, Project Elephant, and Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 play an important role.
ULTRA FINAL REVISION POINTS

items:
• Evergreen – rainfall >200 cm
  • Deciduous – shed leaves
  • Thorn – arid regions
  • Mangroves – aerial roots
  • Tiger – national animal
  • Peacock – national bird
